classification.difficultyReason: Recover an angle from a subdivided straight line and use matching corresponding angles to prove parallelism.

spec.description: Three straight lines CGD, AGF and EGB meet at G. Segment AB closes the lower triangle. No parallel markers, angle arcs or equal-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: Angle EGF = 115 degrees, angle CGA = 30 degrees, angle GBA = 35 degrees. Rays from G use directions 30, 145, 180, 210, 325 and 0 degrees; A and B lie at a shared lower height.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source labels and three numerical givens.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle EGC&=180^\circ-30^\circ-115^\circ\\\angle EGC&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on straight line $AGF$.
$\angle EGC=\angle GBA=35^\circ$.
Therefore $AB\parallel CD$ (converse of the corresponding angle theorem).
